pattern_id: Phantom Finality Anchor (Finalized/Safe points to non-executed block)
description: Many consensus/engine interfaces allow an external component (e.g., consensus client) to set a finalized/safe checkpoint by block hash. If the execution client treats “block is known” as sufficient, a partially persisted (“phantom”) block can be accepted as an anchor even though it is not executable/validated. Once accepted, correct finality rules prevent reorganizing away from that anchor, permanently pinning the node to an invalid/unexecutable fork and causing durable divergence from honest peers (agreement failure) and inability to progress (liveness failure).
trigger_condition: - Implementation accepts consensus “anchor” pointers (finalized/safe/checkpoint) based on block presence (header/body) rather than executed/validated state availability.
